When do Americans do housework and chores?

On an average weekday, the share of Americans doing household tasks peaks at 5:30 PM, when 15.4% of people age 15 and older (about 38.8 million) are doing household tasks. On weekends it peaks at 10:00 AM (19.3%). Averaged over all days, Americans spend 1 hr 51 min a day doing household tasks.

What it includes

Average time per weekday, for the activities in this group that take the most time.

  • Food and drink preparation: 26 min a day
  • Interior cleaning: 19 min a day
  • Lawn, garden, and houseplant care: 10 min a day
  • Laundry: 9 min a day
  • Kitchen and food clean-up: 8 min a day
  • Care for animals and pets (not veterinary care): 7 min a day
  • Household & personal organization and planning: 6 min a day
  • Interior arrangement, decoration, & repairs: 3 min a day

About these numbers

Estimates come from all 258,954 diaries in the American Time Use Survey (Bureau of Labor Statistics and Census Bureau), 2003–2025, weighted to the U.S. civilian population age 15 and older and pooled across years. Times are local clock time. Counts are people on an average day of that type, not a live count. Weekdays are Monday–Friday. How the estimates work.
